values.observations: Two reports were delivered. One customer replied positively. The other has not replied. Time spent producing each report was not recorded.

context.label: Expected evidence
context.value: Understand customer value and the effort needed to produce reports before deciding on a larger rollout.

suggestions.observations: Two reports were delivered. One customer replied positively. The other has not replied. Time spent producing each report was not recorded.
suggestions.difference: No expectation was recorded for the response rate or time spent on report production.
suggestions.learning: The positive response from one customer indicates potential value, but the lack of response from the other customer leaves uncertainty about overall interest. The absence of recorded production time limits understanding of effort versus outcome.
suggestions.nexttest: Record the time spent on producing reports for the next customer engagement and measure the response rate.

questions: What is the expected response rate from customers?
Is there a specific timeframe for when you expect replies from customers?
output.note: Understanding the time investment in report production is crucial for evaluating customer engagement and planning future efforts.
